acme_netops: Hey team — since ~10:40 UTC our Private control-plane connection from our VPC (us-west) times out during the mTLS handshake. App logs show repeated TLS timeouts and curl exits with 56. Anybody seen this pattern?

alice_support: Sorry you hit this — can you paste the openssl s_client output and a short tcpdump (first 100 packets) if possible? Also which control-plane hostname/IP you're hitting?

acme_netops: Hitting control-01.cp.redwood.internal -> 10.24.18.7. Here's the s_client and curl output:

```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.24.18.7:443 -servername control-01.cp.redwood.internal -alpn h2 -tlsextdebug -msg
connect: Connection timed out
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
$ curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://control-01.cp.redwood.internal/health
* About to connect() to 10.24.18.7 port 443
* Trying 10.24.18.7...
* connect to 10.24.18.7 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to 10.24.18.7 port 443: Network is unreachable
```

We also tried from a bastion in same subnet and it succeeds, so looks like egress path from app hosts only.

bob_sre: Interesting — bastion -> success means control plane is fine. Likely something on the host egress path: NAT, firewall, or DPI. Can you run `dig +short @127.0.0.53 control-01.cp.redwood.internal` and `dig +tcp @8.8.8.8 control-01.cp.redwood.internal` and paste results? Also please run `sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap host 10.24.18.7 and port 443` on an affected host and grab the first 100 packets with `-c 100`.

acme_netops: Paste of dig:
```
$ dig +short @127.0.0.53 control-01.cp.redwood.internal
10.24.18.7
$ dig +tcp @8.8.8.8 control-01.cp.redwood.internal
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1-Ubuntu <<>> +tcp @8.8.8.8 control-01.cp.redwood.internal
;; global options: +cmd
;; TCP connection to 8.8.8.8#53(8.8.8.8) for control-01.cp.redwood.internal failed: connection refused
```

Also attaching small tcpdump excerpt: (inline snippet)
```
12:41:03.123456 IP app-host > 10.24.18.7: Flags [S], seq 1001, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
12:41:03.123789 IP 10.24.18.7 > app-host: Flags [S.], seq 2001, ack 1002, win 28960, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 654321 ecr 123456], length 0
12:41:03.124000 IP app-host > 10.24.18.7: Flags [P.], seq 1002:2502, ack 2002, length 1500
12:41:03.124100 IP app-host > 10.24.18.7: Flags [.], seq 2502:4002, ack 2002, length 1500
12:41:03.124200 IP 10.24.18.7 > app-host: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, length 0
```

We see a reset from the control plane sometimes.

dan_neteng: Two quick checks: 1) Do you have an egress firewall or NAT device that does DNS inspection / packet rewriting? 2) What's MTU on the app-host path (run `ip link show` and `ip route get 8.8.8.8`)? Fragmented ClientHello or missing TCP options can cause the server to reject.

acme_netops: We have a corporate egress appliance doing DNS inspection + EDNS trimming. MTU on host appears to be 1400 (we're in a tunneled overlay).

bob_sre: EDNS trimming + small MTU = likely UDP DNS responses being truncated -> resolver falls back or returns wrong CNAME leading to control-plane IP mismatches, or the DPI could be reassembling/rewriting TLS causing RSTs. Two repros for us: (A) DNS path issues where CNAME->IP resolves to a load-balancer that blocks our source IP, (B) TLS inspection device terminating handshake.

alice_support: Can you reproduce with `openssl s_client -connect 10.24.18.7:443 -servername control-01.cp.redwood.internal -msg -tls1_3` from an affected host and capture full 3-way packet capture? If the ClientHello is getting fragmented into multiple IP fragments the control plane's TCP stack might drop it. Also try `curl --resolve control-01.cp.redwood.internal:443:10.24.18.7 -v https://control-01.cp.redwood.internal/health` to bypass DNS.

acme_netops: Ran the resolve trick -> curl succeeds from app-host! So DNS resolution path is definitely in play.

dan_neteng: That nails it: DNS path or response manipulation. The fact `--resolve` works means name->IP mapping from your resolver is returning something wrong on the affected hosts. If DNS inspection truncates EDNS UDP responses and the resolver doesn't fallback to TCP, you can end up with stale or partial records. Action items: allow outbound DNS TCP/UDP to your configured resolvers, or configure your resolver to use DoT/DoH or a reliable upstream. Also check your egress appliance config to avoid rewriting TLS (we see RSTs).

acme_netops: We asked netsec and they confirmed the egress appliance was truncating EDNS and blocking DNS-over-TCP. They also had an MTU mismatch on the NAT causing fragmentation drops. Changed rules to allow DNS TCP (port 53) and patched MTU. After that, connection stabilized.

bob_sre: Great — can you post the `tcpdump -r` snippet showing the final successful handshake so we can close the ticket? Example we want to see: SYN, SYN-ACK, ClientHello (single), ServerHello, Certificate, Finished.

acme_netops: Pasted below — handshake now completes:
```
12:58:01.000000 IP app-host > 10.24.18.7: Flags [S], seq 3001, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 223344 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
12:58:01.000150 IP 10.24.18.7 > app-host: Flags [S.], seq 4001, ack 3002, win 28960, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 998877 ecr 223344], length 0
12:58:01.000300 IP app-host > 10.24.18.7: Flags [P.], seq 3002:4602, ack 4002, length 1600  # ClientHello fits single TLS record
12:58:01.000450 IP 10.24.18.7 > app-host: Flags [P.], seq 4002:7602, ack 4602, length 3600  # ServerHello + certs
12:58:01.000600 IP app-host > 10.24.18.7: Flags [.], seq 4602:4622, ack 7602, length 20   # Finished
```

alice_support: Excellent. I'll mark this as resolved in the ticket. Root cause: egress DNS inspection + EDNS truncation combined with MTU mismatch causing fragmented ClientHello and DPI/NAT resets. Short-term workaround: use `--resolve` or allow DNS/TCP and correct MTU. Long-term: update egress appliance to preserve EDNS and allow TCP fallback, or use secure resolver (DoT/DoH) from your hosts.

depLOY-bot: [case-5241] status changed to resolved by alice_support :white_check_mark:

acme_netops: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage!
